answer: A seat needs a perishable seal. Each applicant presses a numbered brass die into wax cured over an ember bed, signs the notary's book with a quill, and sends the seal by courier across a staffed bridge checkpoint. The notary records the fracture pattern as the seal breaks, then retires that die forever. Every die, crossing and ink entry is single-use, so one operator running a thousand cloned wallets needs a thousand dies, crossings and witnessed signatures, while each seat earns the same flat emission. Sybil cost grows linearly and passes the marginal reward before the registry saturates.
